content:
Manchester United have finalized the acquisition of Manuel Ugarte from Paris Saint-Germain, agreeing on a deal worth €50 million (£42 million) plus an additional €10 million in potential bonuses. The 23-year-old Uruguayan midfielder has committed to a five-year contract, with an option for an extra year. This transfer marks the fifth significant addition to Erik ten Hag’s squad this summer, and it bolsters the team’s midfield with a second experienced defensive midfielder alongside Casemiro.

Ugarte expressed his excitement and determination upon joining one of the world’s most prestigious football clubs. He highlighted the ambition shared by both himself and the club, emphasizing his readiness to work hard and contribute to Manchester United’s pursuit of trophies and a return to the highest level of competition. His enthusiasm for experiencing Old Trafford and dedication to the team’s collective success were evident in his statement.

Dan Ashworth, the club’s sporting director, confirmed that securing Ugarte was a major priority in this transfer window. The club sees him as a key figure in strengthening the squad and supporting Ten Hag’s vision for the team.

With this signing, Manchester United are signaling their intent to challenge more fiercely in domestic and European competitions, aiming to restore the club’s status among football’s elite. The arrival of Ugarte is expected to add depth, resilience, and quality to United’s midfield dynamics.
